meta.title: Mongolian A2 Elementary
meta.subtitle: 750 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Mongolian → English (see the Mongolian, recall the meaning) and English → Mongolian (see an English meaning, recall the Mongolian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 750 words for an elementary learner, aligned to A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance' — a learner here is able to manage simple, routine exchanges of information on familiar matters — personal and family information, shopping, the local area, work — and to describe in simple terms their background, their surroundings and what they immediately need. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no graded Mongolian word list for learners is published under an open licence, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 153 of the 750 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — clothes, the months and the holidays, work and jobs, relatives and the stages of life, feelings, travel, the countryside and the herds, the body and health, food and the kitchen, the things of a home, talking and deciding, the everyday verbs of doing, and describing things — and the other 597 are the commonest remaining words of the Mongolian Wikipedia, counted by the WHOLE word: Mongolian adds its case and tense endings to the word (байшин 'house', байшинд 'in the house', байшингаас 'from the house'; явах 'to go', явна 'goes', явсан 'went'), so those forms are added together. That corpus is encyclopaedic, which shows in the fill (history, government, geography). The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words met most often come first. Only words English Wiktionary has an entry for can be taught here, and some common ones are missing from it (хэцүү 'difficult', эсвэл 'or', хэрэв 'if', буцах 'to return'). Every word is in the Cyrillic alphabet, as Mongolian is written in Mongolia, with no romanisation; the Alphabet deck, first in this collection, teaches the letters. A verb is shown by its dictionary form in -х (явах 'to go'). A noun shows its plural and three of its cases where Wiktionary prints its declension table, and a verb its causative and passive where Wiktionary names them; no form is composed here. Example sentences: 259 of the 750 words have one, from Wiktionary's usage examples and from Tatoeba, which holds about 2,600 Mongolian sentences with a translation; none is invented. There is no speaker button: few devices have a Mongolian voice. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: the Mongolian Wikipedia, articles of the 2026-11-01 dump (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
